answer: In PoA, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph, using stake-weighted transition probabilities and capped influence per path. A sybil cluster may amplify internal endorsements, but its sparse external cut has low conductance, so few walks enter or leave it. Conductance and min-cut transitivity bounds therefore cap its aggregate voting weight, even when it resembles a falcon, reef, or tide of colluding identities.
